title: When...
text:
When

we embrace

we go

to another world

where

we embrace

and march

toward an afterworld

where

we embrace

and where perhaps we only

embrace.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's repeated embrace as a movement into another world and beyond it.

title: Sparrow
text:
It does not forget. It does not leave,

this sly rogue,

our life. Always

borrowed, aimless,

like anyone, it wanders here,

washes itself here, stubborn,

among our shoes.

What does it seek in our dark

living? What love does it find

in our bread so hard?

It has already given the dead

to the air, this sparrow that could

fly, but remains here,

down here, safe,

stuffing into its breast

all the dust of the world.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the sparrow as a low, stubborn witness to human poverty and dust.

title: Pierce Me With Your Eyes, That Cloud
text:
Pierce me with your eyes, that cloud,

and this hope of a man left in me.

Where was I going, if I was in the grove

of your eyes, lying when I was there?


Discipline of everything that rises.

Of what looks and sees, while it tangles

its sad agility, as in the wheel

of your fields of sky I never walked.


And it is from following stainless blindnesses

that so much mist divides us

and makes its marvel from the glare,


its silent carnation. And how strange to harm

we are afterward, when your eyes are the clear

madness of never seeing me always strange!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Rodríguez's difficult syntax, preserving the cloud, blindness, mist, and estranged gaze.

title: Goodbye
text:
Anything would be worth my life

this afternoon. Anything small,

if such a thing exists. Martyrdom to me is the serene

noise, unscrupulous, without return,

of your low shoe. What victories

does the one who loves seek? Why are these streets

so straight? I neither look back nor can I

lose sight of you now. This is the land

of chastening: even friends

give bad information. My mouth kisses

what dies, and accepts it. And the very skin

of the lip is that of the wind. Goodbye. This event

is a useful rule, they say. You remain

with what is ours, you, who can,

for I will go wherever the night wishes.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the farewell's restless movement through streets, love, acceptance, and night.

title: High Wage
text:
Blessed is the one who one fine day goes out humble

and walks along the street, like so many

other days of his life, and does not expect it,

and suddenly, what is this?, looks upward

and sees, puts his ear to the world and hears,

walks, and feels rising between his steps

the love of the earth, and goes on, and opens

his true workshop, and in his hands

his trade shines clean, and he gives it to us

from the heart because he loves, and goes to work

trembling like a child taking communion,

yet unable to fit inside his own skin, and when

he finally realizes how simple

everything has been, the day's wage already earned,

he returns home happy and feels that someone

grips his door knocker, and it is not in vain.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the long sentence of humble work becoming revelation and earned grace.
